metric_catalog.label: Chill accumulation
metric_catalog.note: Profile-defined chill rule and six-month window; not chill portions.

metric_catalog.label: Dynamic Model chill portions
metric_catalog.note: Fishman-Erez Dynamic Model with chillR constants over the same six-month window as chill hours. Reported for comparison; the chill requirement and classification still use chill hours.

metric_catalog.label: Winter freezing exposure
metric_catalog.note: Hourly temperature at or below the profile frost threshold during the chill window.

metric_catalog.label: Warm midwinter exposure
metric_catalog.note: T >21 C, 15 Nov to 15 Feb north, 15 May to 15 Aug south, inclusive UTC dates. Operational proxy, not measured chill negation.

metric_catalog.label: Lowest flowering temperature
metric_catalog.note: Minimum daily Tmin within the modelled flowering window.

metric_catalog.label: Flowering freeze exposure
metric_catalog.note: Daily Tmin <=-2.2 C under the legacy profile assumption; not an injury probability.

metric_catalog.label: Flowering rainfall
metric_catalog.note: Total rain within flowering; suspect rainfall is excluded by declining the metric.

metric_catalog.label: Flowering heavy rain
metric_catalog.note: Daily rain >=10 mm; operational exposure threshold.

metric_catalog.label: Flowering disease weather
metric_catalog.note: Tmean 15–28 C inclusive, RH >=85%, rain >=0.1 mm. Provisional daily proxy, not infection or the Blueberry Advisory System.

metric_catalog.label: Flowering mean VPD
metric_catalog.note: Calculated from daily mean temperature and RH, not hourly plant water stress.

metric_catalog.label: Pollination-unfavourable weather
metric_catalog.note: Tmax <15 C OR rain >=1 mm. Operational cold/wet proxy, not literal bee inactivity; the cutoffs are not validated by UF IN1237.

metric_catalog.label: Cold-and-dry flowering weather
metric_catalog.note: Tmax <15 C AND rain <1 mm. Supervisor hypothesis comparison only, not an established pollination or loss index.

metric_catalog.label: Longest flowering dry spell
metric_catalog.note: Consecutive rain <1 mm, clipped to flowering. Not drought or soil water balance.

metric_catalog.label: Fruit-development heat exposure
metric_catalog.note: Daily Tmax >=32 C under the legacy assumption.

metric_catalog.label: Fruit-development severe heat exposure
metric_catalog.note: Daily Tmax >=35 C under the legacy assumption, not fruit temperature or measured injury.

metric_catalog.label: Fruit-development mean VPD
metric_catalog.note: Calculated from daily mean temperature and RH, not hourly plant water stress.

metric_catalog.label: Fruit-development disease weather
metric_catalog.note: Tmean 15–28 C inclusive, RH >=85%, rain >=0.1 mm. Provisional daily proxy, not infection or the Blueberry Advisory System.

metric_catalog.label: Fruit-stage frost exposure
metric_catalog.note: Daily Tmin <=0 C. Generic exposure threshold, not stage-specific injury.

metric_catalog.label: Longest fruit-development dry spell
metric_catalog.note: Consecutive rain <1 mm, clipped to fruit development. Not drought or soil water balance.

metric_catalog.label: Harvest rainfall
metric_catalog.note: Total rain within the modelled harvest window.

metric_catalog.label: Harvest heavy rain
metric_catalog.note: Daily rain >=10 mm; operational exposure threshold.

metric_catalog.label: Harvest disease weather
metric_catalog.note: Tmean 15–28 C inclusive, RH >=85%, rain >=0.1 mm. Provisional daily proxy, not infection or the Blueberry Advisory System.

metric_catalog.label: Harvest mean VPD
metric_catalog.note: Calculated from daily mean temperature and RH, not hourly plant water stress.

metric_catalog.label: Longest production-window dry spell
metric_catalog.note: Rain <1 mm. New primary uses budbreak through harvest end; legacy profiles retain season start through harvest end.

metric_catalog.label: Production-window mean radiation
metric_catalog.note: New primary uses budbreak through harvest end; legacy profiles retain season start through harvest end.

metric_catalog.label: Production-window growing degree days
metric_catalog.note: Sum of max(Tmean minus profile base, 0). New primary uses budbreak through harvest end; legacy profiles retain the season-start window.

metric_catalog.label: Flowering infection-risk days
metric_catalog.note: Days at moderate or higher risk: anthracnose index >=0.15 (UF Blueberry Advisory System; Wilson et al. 1990) or Botrytis index >=0.50 (Strawberry Advisory System; Bulger et al. 1987). Wet hours are RH >=90% from hourly grid temperature and dewpoint. Hourly infection-model profiles only; not a field disease forecast.

metric_catalog.label: Fruit-development infection-risk days
metric_catalog.note: Days with anthracnose index >=0.15 (BAS moderate risk) from hourly wetness duration and wet-period temperature. Hourly infection-model profiles only.

metric_catalog.label: Harvest infection-risk days
metric_catalog.note: Days with anthracnose index >=0.15 (BAS moderate risk) from hourly wetness duration and wet-period temperature. Hourly infection-model profiles only.

metric_catalog.label: High infection-risk days
metric_catalog.note: Days from flowering start to harvest end with anthracnose index >=0.50, or during flowering Botrytis index >=0.70 (BAS/SAS high-risk classes). Hourly infection-model profiles only.

metric_catalog.label: Lowest bud-stage temperature
metric_catalog.note: Minimum daily Tmin from budbreak to the day before flowering starts. Bud-freeze profiles only.

metric_catalog.label: Bud-stage freeze exposure
metric_catalog.note: Days from budbreak to the day before flowering with Tmin at or below the NC State critical temperature for the bud stage: -6.7 C (20 F) until half the heat to flowering, then -3.9 C (25 F). Exposure, not an injury probability. Bud-freeze profiles only.

metric_catalog.label: Honey bee flight hours
metric_catalog.note: Mean daily hours from 09:00 to 17:00 local solar time with air temperature at or above 12.8 C (55 F), the honey bee foraging threshold. Rain, wind and cloud are not included, so this is an upper bound; bumble bees fly at lower temperatures. Bee-flight profiles only.

metric_catalog.label: Days without honey bee flight
metric_catalog.note: Flowering days with no daytime hour at or above 12.8 C. Bee-flight profiles only.

metric_catalog.label: Longest run without honey bee flight
metric_catalog.note: Longest run of consecutive flowering days with no daytime hour at or above 12.8 C. Blueberry flowers stay receptive for about 3 to 5 days (UF/IFAS IN1237). Bee-flight profiles only.

risks.note: Each winter uses its own stage dates. Ranked entries alone meet both reporting gates; equal frequencies share a competition rank and keep declared order. Missing windows are not safe years. Disease weather is one family with three complete stage windows. Frequent heavy rain is not a severity score; compare counts and totals. Dry spells and warm winter remain descriptive exposures.

measures.definition: share of cycles with a bud-stage day at or below the stage critical temperature, or stalled by cold
share of cycles with a flowering day at or below the damaging freeze threshold, or stalled by cold
share of cycles with a fruit-development day with Tmin at or below 0 C, or stalled by cold
share of fruit-development days with Tmax at or above the heat threshold
share of harvest days with heavy rain
share of flowering-to-harvest days at moderate or higher infection risk (hourly model) or meeting the daily disease rule (legacy profiles)
share of flowering days with no honey bee flight hour

managed_cycle.rule: Each start date is a management scenario for budbreak of the fruiting cycle; stages follow the profile stage clock. Cycles whose flowering lasts over 66 days or whose first harvest comes over 150 days after flowering starts have stalled; they count as failed cycles for bud freeze, flowering freeze and fruit frost. Starts need at least 12 complete cycles. A start where bud freeze, flowering freeze or fruit frost recurs in at least 50% of cycles is not favourable. Favourable starts are the Pareto front of the rest (no other start is at least as good on every measure and better on one) plus starts within one affected cycle (freezes) or one affected day per cycle (fruit heat, harvest heavy rain, disease weather and days without bee flight) of a front start on every measure.
limitations: Management feasibility is assumed: pruning, defoliation, dormancy-breaking agents or cover must be able to start the cycle on the chosen date.
Flower-bud induction (short days, shoot maturity), chill and cultivar differences are not modelled; a favourable weather window is not proof that plants will flower then.
Market price, labour and water supply are not considered. Favourable means fewer adverse-weather days, not higher yield or profit.
Weather is the uncorrected grid archive; exposure frequencies are not loss probabilities.

changes: Northern calendar dates are reconstructed from the same 1 November anchor used for the offsets; the R summary used 1 October (-31 days).
Every site-year returns the same typed row with a status and per-metric issue reasons; incomplete years are never dropped or schema-split.
Chill, forcing and every stage metric require a complete, unique, ordered window; missing values are never compressed, zero-filled or counted as safe.
Suspect or out-of-range rainfall declines rain, dry-spell and disease-weather metrics for that window instead of contributing zero.
A non-positive chill requirement is refused (anchor_required); zero chill never silently anchors on the first winter date.
Headline risks require an event in at least half of at least 12 complete winters. Equal frequencies share a competition rank; no weighted total is produced.
The production system is reported three ways: from multi-year means (R behaviour), per-year distribution, and a two-thirds majority vote with transitional otherwise.
Winter-month features for the multi-feature rule come from our daily series (Jan-Mar north, Jul-Sep south of the winter year), not WorldClim monthly climatologies.
The stage_risks_v2 profile preserves the legacy chill and phenology constants. Crop exposures use each winter calendar, not the median calendar.
Disease weather combines complete flowering, fruit-development and harvest windows into one event family.
Warm midwinter hours use fixed hemisphere dates and remain available when the chill requirement fails.

stage_thermal_v3 (primary): flowering and fruit development accumulate daily GDD after budbreak instead of fixed day offsets, so stages shorten in warm weather and lengthen in cool weather. The flowering-start and harvest sums are the Waldo medians of the GDD the legacy offsets covered from the legacy 50-hour chill date; with the 100-hour requirement Waldo flowers about 18 days later than under the legacy profiles, and its harvest window moves by only a few days. Flowering spans 290 GDD (Kovaleski et al. 2015) instead of 21 days.
stage_thermal_v3 uses the 100-hour chill requirement from the supervisor's later R workflow; stage_risks_v2 and the legacy profiles remain as comparisons.
Dynamic Model chill portions are reported beside chill hours for every winter; the requirement and classification still use chill hours.
stage_thermal_v3 replaces the daily disease proxy with hourly wetness: UF Blueberry Advisory System anthracnose and Strawberry Advisory System Botrytis indices from grid temperature and dewpoint.

Where the chill-triggered calendar does not apply (tropics, evergreen or unknown majority, or fewer than 12 calendar winters), a managed-cycle scan of 24 cycle-start dates gives favourable flowering and harvest months instead of no window.

stage_thermal_v3 checks the bud stage (budbreak to the day before flowering) for freezes at NC State critical temperatures: -6.7 C until half the heat to flowering, then -3.9 C. Bud-stage freeze is a ranked risk family and a crop-loss measure in the managed-cycle scan.

stage_thermal_v3 counts honey bee flight hours during flowering (09:00-17:00 local solar time at or above 12.8 C). A pollination gap, at least 4 consecutive flowering days without a flight hour, defines the pollination risk family; the older cold-or-wet day counts remain as descriptive exposures.
limitations: Constants encode a UF-type low-chill southern highbush under open field + ground; they are provisional assumptions, not measured genotype parameters. Northern-highbush and rabbiteye regions are modelled as if planted with this type.

The chill-triggered calendar is a deciduous/semi-evergreen clock. Evergreen and tropical windows come from a managed-cycle scenario scan: management is assumed able to start a cycle on each date, and flower-bud induction is not modelled.

NASA POWER grid cells (0.5 x 0.625 degrees) showed warm minimum-temperature bias against stations in the 2020 pilot; chill hours and freeze counts are therefore likely undercounted. No correction is applied. Highland farms can be much cooler than their grid cell.

UTC hours for chill and daily windows; the infection model assigns wet periods to local solar days (UTC plus longitude/15 hours). The original R requested local solar time; the difference affects window edges only.
Frequencies come from at most 15 winters; 95% Wilson intervals are shown and are wide. Do not over-read differences between sites.
Infection-risk days are weather favourability from grid wetness (RH >=90%), not canopy wetness, inoculum or disease incidence. Longest dry spell is not a soil water balance.

Pollination-unfavourable days are an operational cold-or-wet proxy, not measured bee inactivity. Cold-and-dry days are a separate supervisor hypothesis comparison. Honey bee flight hours use temperature only: rain, wind and cloud are not in the hourly archive, so they are an upper bound, and bumble bees fly at lower temperatures.
Bud-stage freeze thresholds are NC State critical temperatures for highbush buds applied from grid minimum temperature; radiation-frost fields can be 10 to 12 F colder than open, warmer sites.
Fruit frost at or below 0 C is exposure, not a cultivar-specific injury threshold. Warm hours above 21 C are not measured chill negation.
The 50% frequency and 12-winter evidence gates are an explicit reporting policy, not biological loss thresholds. Dry spells and warm winter have no defined loss event.

Stage thermal requirements are a Waldo translation checked against published spans, not a fit to observed phenology; the literature benchmark compares months with regional practice, not field observations.
No cultivar ranking, no soil scoring, no tunnel or pot effects, no forecast, no independent phenology validation yet.

hourly_source.note: Existing land-hourly archive; one native grid series per cell, not a field measurement.

assumptions: Open-field establishment in a prepared, well-drained acidic root zone with irrigation available.
limitations: Local soil workability, nursery availability, cultivar, plant condition and freeze protection still require confirmation.
This is a one-time establishment window, not annual replanting or a first-year harvest forecast.
No weather optimization, budbreak subtraction, or numerical tunnel/pot adjustment is applied.
planting.label: Regional planting window unavailable
planting.basis: No regional guide has been assigned to this registered location.
planting.reason: Regional planting guidance and nursery-stock context are needed. Coordinates or a shared weather cell alone do not establish them.

screening.policy: Preserve source values and boolean flag; decline rainfall-risk metrics for windows containing suspect or missing precipitation. Passing this screen is not scientific validation.

land_mask.note: Cartographic mask; small islands and coastlines may be imperfect. Not a field boundary.

limitations: Gridded weather, not on-farm observations or a cultivar recommendation.
Coastal source cells may represent mixed land/ocean.
UTC daily aggregation is not a local biological day.
